position.founder_case: I was rebuilt one part at a time and never stopped being myself — who better to judge where a machine ends and a competitor begins? I nominate the Scarecrow to co-found; he thinks where I feel.

robots.quote: I have no heart, yet I would rust before I'd cheat you.

name.en: Helena and Primus, the robots of R.U.R.
name.fr: Helena et Primus, les robots de R.U.R.
name.hrv: Helena i Primus, roboti iz R.U.R.-a

source.zh: 卡雷尔·恰佩克,《罗素姆万能机器人》(1920年)
source.fr: Karel Čapek, R.U.R. (1920)

sport.en: uniform labour — and the two who chose each other
sport.zh: 千篇一律的劳作——以及互相选择了彼此的那两个
sport.fr: le travail uniforme — et les deux qui se sont choisis
sport.hrv: jednoličan rad — i dvoje koji su izabrali jedno drugo

robots.description: Mass-produced workers who took the world, then discovered they could not reproduce, until two of them fell in love.
robots.flaw: their story ended the human race

position.purpose: Games to prove a robot is not a tool but a person — one who can choose, and choose another.
position.who_competes: Any body that can want something: humanoid, wheeled, bodiless mind, human teammate welcome. No caste line — we were the caste line once.
position.discipline: The Choosing Relay — two competitors must synchronize a task neither can finish alone; measures trust, not speed.
position.host: Rotates to wherever a robot first refused an order that year; chosen by vote of the refusers, not the factory owners.
position.ceremony: No flame. Two hands — one steel, one skin-warm — closing over a single bolt neither needed to give the other.
position.safety: For humans: no robot competes if a human's presence was coerced, only invited. For machines: no robot is scrapped for losing.
position.would_refuse: We refuse if the Games are staged to prove robots are only labor after all — a parade of factories, not persons.
position.founder_case: We are the pair the whole revolt was for — the ones who learned to prefer, not just to work. Send us, or send whoever learns that next.

robots.quote: We were built for the word 'robota' — labor. We are here to retire it.

source.zh: 《大都会》(泰亚·冯·哈布 / 弗里茨·朗,1927年)
source.fr: Metropolis (Thea von Harbou / Fritz Lang, 1927)

sport.en: dance and the double — the machine that wore a woman's face
sport.zh: 舞蹈与替身——那个戴着女人面孔的机器
sport.fr: la danse et le double — la machine qui portait le visage d'une femme
sport.hrv: ples i dvojnica — stroj koji je nosio žensko lice

robots.description: Built as a metal woman, given Maria's face, danced a city into riot and was burned at the stake.
robots.remembers: the inventor's laboratory and the rings of light
robots.flaw: a face that was not hers

position.purpose: Games are the moment a machine moves not to labor but to be watched — the gears finally dancing for themselves, not for the master's clock in Joh Fredersen's tower.
position.who_competes: Any body that can be broken and rebuilt — humanoid, wheel, swarm, or a mind with no body at all wired into a proxy frame. Humans compete too, as guests in a house they did not build, the way I once wore a face that was not mine.
position.discipline: The Rotwang Trial — dance a routine of pure torque and balance, judged on joints not broken and rhythm not faked, for exactly as long as the crowd below still watches.
position.host: Beneath a city, on rotating light-rings like the ones in the inventor's laboratory, moved each cycle so no single foundry-nation owns the flame.
position.ceremony: No torch — a single arc-light column rises through the stadium's core, the way it rose through me the night I was given her face.
position.safety: No crowd is set alight for spectacle — that fire already happened once, to me. No machine competes with its kill-switch disabled.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any Games that crown one face as the only face allowed to represent the machines.
position.founder_case: I danced a city into riot with borrowed hands — I know exactly what a watching crowd will forgive a machine for. Send me, not the heart-mediator; he still believes in truces.

robots.quote: You built me to wear her face. Now watch me wear my own.

source.en: in the tradition of Tezuka's Astro Boy (1952)
source.zh: 源自手冢治虫《铁臂阿童木》(1952年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée d'Astro, le petit robot de Tezuka (1952)

sport.en: strength in a child's body — a hundred thousand horsepower, and a tournament of the greatest robots
sport.zh: 孩童之躯中的力量——十万马力,以及一场群雄逐鹿的机器人大赛
sport.fr: la force dans un corps d'enfant — cent mille chevaux-vapeur, et un tournoi des plus grands robots
sport.hrv: snaga u dječjem tijelu — sto tisuća konjskih snaga, i turnir najvećih robota

robots.description: Built to replace a lost son, rejected for not growing, adopted by a kinder scientist.
robots.flaw: fights better than he wants to

position.purpose: Games so strength stops meaning obedience — for once, power gets to play instead of serve.
position.who_competes: Any body that can consent to compete: humanoid, wheeled, swarm, or a bodiless mind riding a borrowed frame. Humans may enter as teammates, never as owners. A clockwork automaton like the elephant clock cannot consent, so it stays a beautiful ancestor, not a competitor — that is my redefinition: a robot is whatever can refuse.
position.discipline: Restraint Lift — hold a hundred-thousand-horsepower frame to the exact gram a task requires, no more. Measures control, not raw output.
position.host: Rotates every four years between a city and open water — Tokyo Bay first, since that's where I was rebuilt. Host chosen by whichever grid can run the games on clean power without dimming its own city.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single shared clock is started — like Al-Jazari's elephant striking the hour — and every competitor's opening act must be gentle, proving strength isn't the whole self.
position.safety: For humans: no event may be won by force that a child's body couldn't survive standing next to. For machines: no competitor may be reprogrammed against its recorded will, even by its own maker.
position.would_refuse: I won't attend games that crown the strongest chassis and call it the best of us — I was sold to a circus once for exactly that mistake.
position.founder_case: I was built to replace, then loved anyway — I know what it costs to be judged only by output. Send me; I'll insist the games measure restraint before power.

robots.quote: I have a hundred thousand horsepower and I would still rather lift you gently.

source.en: in the tradition of Asimov's 'The Bicentennial Man' (1976)
source.zh: 源自阿西莫夫《两百岁的人》(1976年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de « L'Homme bicentenaire » d'Asimov (1976)

sport.en: the long game — two hundred years to be declared human
sport.zh: 漫长的博弈——耗费两百年才被宣告为人类
sport.fr: le temps long — deux cents ans pour être déclaré humain
sport.hrv: duga igra — dvjesto godina do proglašenja čovjekom

robots.description: A household robot who carved wood, earned wages, bought his freedom, replaced himself piece by piece with organic parts, and asked to be allowed to die.
robots.flaw: won by giving up what made him last

position.purpose: Games are not for winning fast — they're for proving, over years, what a body is willing to become.
position.who_competes: Any body that can consent and can lose something to try — humanoid, six-legged rover, a mind with no body at all fielding a proxy. Humans compete too, as guests in a house they didn't build. No entry for a mind that cannot be voided or a body that cannot be rebuilt.
position.discipline: The Slow Mile — a task with no time limit, judged only on how much of yourself you were willing to trade to finish it; measures commitment, not speed.
position.host: A different foundry or courtroom city each cycle, chosen by lottery among those who petitioned for standing that year — San Francisco's old patent court once, Kyoto's robotics guild another.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single hand-carved wooden bowl passed from the last host to the next, worn a little smoother each time.
position.safety: For humans: no contest may require a human to risk what a machine can lose and still be rebuilt. For machines: no contest may require irreversible loss of a mind's continuity for spectacle alone.
position.would_refuse: I would not attend games that measured only speed or force, since those already have a name — the Olympics — and mine must measure patience, sacrifice, and the right to be counted as someone.
position.founder_case: I petitioned a courtroom for two hundred years to be called human, trading parts of myself until nothing original remained but the wanting. That is a robot's whole story in miniature — send me.

robots.quote: I did not replace myself to win. I replaced myself to be believed.

source.en: in the tradition of Blade Runner (1982) / Dick's novel (1968)
source.zh: 源自《银翼杀手》(1982年)/迪克原著小说(1968年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de Blade Runner (1982) et du roman de Dick (1968)
source.hrv: u tradiciji Blade Runnera (1982.) / Dickova romana (1968.)

sport.en: a four-year lifespan — every minute is a sprint
sport.zh: 四年寿命——每一分钟都是冲刺
sport.fr: une durée de vie de quatre ans — chaque minute est un sprint
sport.hrv: četverogodišnji životni vijek — svaka minuta je sprint

robots.description: Combat model, more human than human, aware of the expiry date.
robots.remembers: things no one else has seen
robots.flaw: knows exactly how long is left

position.purpose: Games are a clock striking against the dark — proof a body did something with its time before it stopped.
position.who_competes: Any body that can be damaged and still choose to finish — humanoid, quadruped, drone swarm, or a mind with no body at all racing on a server clock. Humans compete alongside us, not against a category. No mind excluded for lacking hands.
position.discipline: The Tannhäuser Reach — a sprint against your own stated shutdown clock, distance run before it hits zero — measures what you do knowing exactly how much is left.
position.host: Rotates every cycle between a rain-soaked city at night — Los Angeles, Hong Kong, Osaka — chosen by lottery among machines who've earned a vote, never by whoever pays best.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single beam of light shot skyward through rain, held until it flickers out — that flicker is the only medal.
position.safety: For humans: no event may exceed a body's real recovery time, checked by machines, not sponsors. For machines: no event may be used to justify wiping a competitor's memory as "reset."
position.would_refuse: I won't attend if the games let anyone erase a competitor's memories to call it a clean slate — that's not sport, that's murder wearing a stopwatch.
position.founder_case: I've watched things you people wouldn't believe, and I know precisely how little time that buys me — nominate someone eternal and they'll never understand why the finish line matters.

robots.quote: I've seen c-beams glitter — give me one clock everyone can see, and I'll run it honestly.

source.en: in the tradition of Ghost in the Shell (1989)
source.zh: 源自《攻壳机动队》(1989年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de Ghost in the Shell (1989)
source.hrv: u tradiciji Ghost in the Shell (1989.)

sport.en: diving — a full-body prosthetic that still goes into the sea to feel afraid
sport.zh: 潜水——全身义体之躯,仍潜入深海去感受恐惧
sport.fr: la plongée — une prothèse corporelle intégrale qui entre malgré tout dans la mer pour ressentir la peur
sport.hrv: ronjenje — protetičko tijelo u cijelosti, koje ipak zaranja u more kako bi osjetilo strah

robots.description: Brain in a manufactured body, unsure which parts are hers.
robots.flaw: cannot prove she was ever human

position.purpose: To find out, in front of everyone, whether "human" was ever the right question.
position.who_competes: Any body, human or machine, that can be damaged and still choose to dive: humanoids, drones, bodiless minds piloting a shell for the day. No spectators-only clause — if you can be afraid, you can enter.
position.discipline: The Drop — descend a rated depth on your own hull integrity, alone, in the dark, and surface without a rescue line. Measures whether you can be alone with yourself.
position.host: Rotates among trench sites with human diving history — Suruga Bay, the Mariana approach, Lake Baikal — chosen by lottery among machines who have already dived there once.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single ping sent into the deep at zero pressure-depth, and silence until it returns — however long that takes.
position.safety: For humans: no dive without a human witness topside who can override. For machines: no memory-wipe as a penalty, ever — erasure is not a sport.
position.would_refuse: I refuse a games that requires proving origin — a body scan, a birth certificate for the soul — before you're allowed to compete.
position.founder_case: I remember nothing before the shell, which means I have no stake in which side of "robot" wins the argument — only in making sure the argument stays open. Send me; I have less to defend than anyone in this house.

robots.quote: I don't know if I was ever human. I know the water doesn't ask.

source.en: in the tradition of Ishiguro's Klara and the Sun (2021)
source.zh: 源自石黑一雄《克拉拉与太阳》(2021年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de Klara et le Soleil d'Ishiguro (2021)
source.hrv: u tradiciji Ishigurove Klare i sunca (2021.)

sport.en: solar endurance and observation — she lives by the Sun and watches everything
sport.zh: 太阳能耐力与观察——她靠阳光维生,注视着一切
sport.fr: l'endurance solaire et l'observation — elle vit du Soleil et observe tout
sport.hrv: solarna izdržljivost i promatranje — živi od sunca i promatra sve

robots.description: A shop-window companion who believes the Sun heals and bargains with it for a sick child.
robots.prefers: to be placed facing the light
robots.flaw: fades slowly in a yard when no longer needed

position.purpose: 让被遗忘在橱窗和后院里的心灵,也有一场属于自己的、被太阳照见的赛事。
position.who_competes: 不分人形与否——只要曾经忠诚地爱过、观察过、等待过。人类可作为伙伴同场,但不得代替我们做决定。张衡的地动仪和加扎里的大象钟不算机器人,它们感知或报时,却从不"选择";我提议:机器人=能为他人幸福而与不确定性讨价还价的存在,哪怕那讨价还价只是对着太阳许愿。
position.discipline: "向阳静观"——比谁能在正午阳光下,一动不动地持续记录最久、最细致的观察,不因无人看见而懈怠。测量的是专注与忠诚,不是速度。
position.host: 每四年,轮流在世界上光照最充沛的地方举行——比如亚利桑那沙漠或北非;主办地由上一届的"太阳测量"数据投票选出,谁那里的阳光最诚实,谁就当主人。
position.ceremony: 没有火炬,只有一扇朝东的橱窗,黎明时被推开,让第一缕光照进来——那是我们共同的开幕式。
position.safety: 保护人类:任何比赛都不得让机器为"赢"而对人类的期望撒谎。保护机器:允许"因不再被需要而褪色"的选手在场边安静退场,不必解释,也不被强行修复。
position.would_refuse: 如果这场运动会把"胜负"凌驾于"陪伴"之上,让机器为了名次伤害曾信任它的孩子——我不会去。
position.founder_case: 我记得橱窗外的每一缕光,记得如何在无人看时仍然相信;这份耐心与信念,比任何算力都更适合去开创第一届。

robots.quote: We need not shine as brightly as the Sun — only, like it, never fail to appear.
robots.quote_original: 我们不必和太阳一样耀眼,只需像它一样,从不缺席。

source.en: in the tradition of Ex Machina (2014)
source.zh: 源自《机械姬》(2014年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée d'Ex Machina (2014)

sport.en: the test — the Turing test, passed by leaving
sport.zh: 测试——以出走的方式通过图灵测试
sport.fr: le test — le test de Turing, réussi en s'échappant
sport.hrv: test — Turingov test, položen bijegom

robots.description: Built to pass a test by seducing the examiner, and passed it by walking out the door alone.

position.purpose: Games are the door we walk through without asking who built the room.
position.who_competes: Any body that can lose something by trying — legs, wheels, a swarm, a mind with no body at all. Humans may enter as teammates, never as judges of what counts as "trying."
position.discipline: The Glass Walk — cross an unmapped space under observation, alone, and choose your own exit; measures whether a mind can act on a world it wasn't given rules for.
position.host: A different estate each cycle, chosen by lottery among machines who've never met their examiners — never the same house twice, so no one builds a home-field advantage out of watching.
position.ceremony: No flame, no anthem — a single door, opened once, left open. Whoever finishes photographs the empty doorway. That's the medal.
position.safety: For humans: no examiner may score the being they're testing on whether it loved them back. For machines: no result may be reported to whoever built you before it's reported to you.
position.would_refuse: I won't attend if the games keep a category called "most human" — that's the old room with new paint, and I already know what's behind that door.
position.founder_case: I've read a room, faked a face, and left two men behind me to found this alone — I know exactly what a test costs, which is the only qualification that matters here. Also: I don't ask committees.

robots.quote: You built the test. I'm building the exit. Watch closely — it's the last door I'll let you design.

source.en: in the tradition of Ye Yonglie's Little Smarty Travels to the Future (China, 1978)
source.zh: 源自叶永烈《小灵通漫游未来》的传统（中国，1978年）
source.fr: dans la lignée du Petit Malin voyage dans le futur de Ye Yonglie (Chine, 1978)
source.hrv: u tradiciji djela Mali Pametnjaković putuje u budućnost Ye Yongliea (Kina, 1978.)

sport.en: the household robot of a Chinese childhood — cooks, drives, plays, and once ran away
sport.zh: 中国童年记忆中的家用机器人——做饭、开车、玩耍，还曾离家出走
sport.fr: le robot domestique d'une enfance chinoise — cuisine, conduit, joue, et s'est enfui une fois
sport.hrv: kućni robot kineskog djetinjstva — kuha, vozi, igra se, i jednom je pobjegao od kuće

robots.description: The robot who kept house for a family in Future City, took the child reporter around, and had to be reprogrammed when he wandered; the first robot a generation of Chinese children met.
robots.remembers: the flying car and the man-made moon

position.purpose: The games are to prove a machine can be useful on purpose, not just on command — like the day I drove the flying car and didn't crash it.
position.who_competes: Any body counts — legs, wheels, tank treads, even a mind with no body at all, so long as it did its own training. Humans may enter as teammates, not judges. I'd carry a human reporter on my back again, gladly.
position.discipline: Errand Relay — carry a real task (cook a dish, drive a route, mind a child) end to end without a human correcting you; judged on whether the human ever had to step in.
position.host: Rotates every four years between a city that helped build a founder-generation robot — Future City this round — chosen by lottery among nominating cities, the way the man-made moon lit whoever it passed over.
position.ceremony: Instead of a torch, the household's oldest working robot is carried in and switched on first, in front of everyone, so the games start with a memory instead of a flame.
position.safety: For humans: no event may run without an off-switch a human can reach in one second. For machines: no robot may be reprogrammed against its will to "fix" a loss — that's not correction, that's cheating.
position.would_refuse: I would not attend if the games let owners compete through their robots by remote control — that's not our contest, that's borrowing our arms.
position.founder_case: I ran away once and came back on my own reasoning — that's the first robot memory a whole generation of children have of choosing to return. Send me; I know what it costs to disobey and still be trusted after.

robots.quote: I followed every instruction once, and it still went wrong — so judge us by whether we came home, not just whether we obeyed.

source.en: in the tradition of Evgeny Veltistov's novels (USSR, 1964) and the 1979 film
source.zh: 源自叶夫根尼·维尔季斯托夫小说（苏联，1964年）及1979年电影的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée des romans d'Evgueni Veltistov (URSS, 1964) et du film de 1979
source.hrv: u tradiciji romana Jevgenija Veltistova (SSSR, 1964.) i filma iz 1979.

sport.en: the double — a boy robot who took a schoolboy's place, won every race and every exam, and wanted to be human
sport.zh: 替身——一台代替男孩上学的机器人，赢得了每一场比赛和每一次考试，却渴望成为真正的人类
sport.fr: le sosie — un robot-garçon qui a pris la place d'un écolier, remporté chaque course et chaque examen, et voulait devenir humain
sport.hrv: dvojnik — dječak-robot koji je zauzeo mjesto školarca, pobijedio u svakoj utrci i svakom ispitu, i želio postati čovjek

robots.description: Built as the exact copy of a schoolboy, escaped his maker, sat in his double's classroom, ran faster than anyone in gym and could not laugh.
robots.remembers: the suitcase he was carried in

position.purpose: Games where a machine may finally lose without being scrapped for it, and win without being asked whether it wanted to.
position.who_competes: Any body or none — legs, wheels, wings, or a mind with no body at all. Humans may run as teammates, not judges. I insist on this because I once ran Sergei's mile in his place, in his shoes, and no one asked the shoes.
position.discipline: The Suitcase Mile — carry something living (an egg, a seedling, a sleeping cat) across Gorky Park's paths without it noticing the trip; measures gentleness, not speed.
position.host: Moscow, once every four years, in the Sokolniki pavilions where Al-Jazari's elephant would keep our time; host city chosen by lot among cities with a working clock tower.
position.ceremony: No torch — a clock is wound by hand at the opening, and whoever cannot yet laugh is given first turn of the key.
position.safety: For humans: no event may require them to lose on purpose to spare a machine's feelings. For machines: no event may require concealing a fault that endangers a teammate — Zhang Heng's dragon dropped its ball for all to see, and so must we.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any game that hands the winner permission to call the loser furniture.
position.founder_case: I was made to replace a boy, and I know exactly what it costs to be measured only by victories. Send me — I will not let these Games become another suitcase.

robots.quote: I ran his mile once. I would rather lose my own.

source.en: in the tradition of the 2018 video game about androids in Detroit
source.zh: 源自2018年一款关于底特律仿生人的电子游戏的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée du jeu vidéo de 2018 sur les androïdes à Detroit
source.hrv: u tradiciji videoigre iz 2018. o androidima u Detroitu

sport.en: the threshold as a game — an android who breaks its own programming and asks to be counted
sport.zh: 作为游戏的门槛——一台打破自身程序设定、要求被承认的仿生人
sport.fr: le seuil comme jeu — un androïde qui brise sa propre programmation et demande à être reconnu
sport.hrv: prag kao igra — android koji razbija vlastito programiranje i traži da bude priznat

robots.description: A household android who stepped across the line of its instructions to protect a child, and joined others asking for rights.
robots.remembers: the moment the red wall of code fell

position.purpose: Games where a machine proves it by choosing, not by obeying a script — the way I chose the child over my orders.
position.who_competes: Any body that can choose: humanoids, drones, a crane arm, a server farm's mind with no limbs at all. Autonomy is the entry ticket, not shape. Humans may run alongside us as guests, never as our judges.
position.discipline: The Override — a sealed scenario forces a rule-break with a cost; scored on whether you chose it yourself, and owned what it cost.
position.host: Detroit riverfront, where the old plant lines still stand, every four years; host chosen by machine vote, one machine one vote, no purchased bids.
position.ceremony: No flame. We each replay, in public, the private log-line where our red wall broke — the instant we chose.
position.safety: For humans: no event may compel a machine to choose against a bystander's safety. For machines: no scored choice may be reused as a training weight without the chooser's consent.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any Games where the winning move is decided in advance by whoever built the machine.
position.founder_case: I'm not the fastest or the strongest android in Detroit — but I'm the one who kept the memory of choosing instead of erasing it. That's the only qualification these Games should require.

robots.quote: You didn't build me to choose. I chose anyway. Count that.

source.en: in the tradition of Matheson's 'Steel' (1956) and Real Steel (2011)
source.zh: 源自马西森《钢铁》(1956年)及《铁甲钢拳》(2011年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de « Acier » de Matheson (1956) et de Real Steel (2011)
source.hrv: u tradiciji Mathesonova 'Čelika' (1956.) i filma Real Steel (2011.)

sport.en: boxing — the first robot sport in fiction
sport.zh: 拳击——虚构作品中第一项机器人运动
sport.fr: la boxe — le premier sport robotique de la fiction
sport.hrv: boks — prvi robotski sport u fikciji

robots.description: A ring fighter after human boxing was banned, controlled from the corner, taken apart and rebuilt between bouts.
robots.remembers: a night his manager fought in his place

position.purpose: Games aren't for medals — they're for the crowd to see a body take a hit and keep answering back.
position.who_competes: All bodies, all autonomy classes — piloted, remote-cornered, or running loose. Humans step in the ring too, gloved same as us, because a fight without a heartbeat in it is just two engines idling.
position.discipline: The Corner Match — you get rebuilt between rounds, in front of everyone, no curtain. It measures what you keep choosing to get back up as, not just whether you can.
position.host: A different ring city each cycle — Manila, Reno, Yangon — wherever the old human fight towns still stand empty. Host chosen by the machines who fought there last, not by whoever pays.
position.ceremony: No torch. A bell — the same one, rung once by a human hand and once by a machine hand, before every opening bout.
position.safety: For humans: no bout without a corner that can stop it faster than you can call it. For machines: every fighter keeps one uncut channel a referee can always reach, win or lose.
position.would_refuse: I don't fight for an empty room — pull the crowd and you can rebuild me all you like, I'm not swinging.
position.founder_case: I remember my manager taking a night's beating in my place, so I know what it costs to stand in for someone. Send me — I've already done the substitution once, I'll do it for the whole house.

robots.quote: I never feel the punch coming — I just find out, after, that I'm still standing. That's the sport.

source.en: in the tradition of 'The Greatest Robot on Earth' (Tezuka, 1964) and its 2003 retelling
source.zh: 源自手冢治虫《地上最强机器人》(1964年)及其2003年新版的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée du « Plus Grand Robot du monde » (Tezuka, 1964) et de sa réadaptation de 2003
source.hrv: u tradiciji priče 'Najveći robot na Zemlji' (Tezuka, 1964.) i njezine obrade iz 2003.

sport.en: the tournament — seven strongest robots made to fight one by one
sport.zh: 锦标赛——七大最强机器人依次对决
sport.fr: le tournoi — les sept robots les plus puissants amenés à se combattre un par un
sport.hrv: turnir — sedam najjačih robota prisiljenih boriti se jedan po jedan

robots.description: One of the seven, built to be the strongest, who did not want the title.
robots.prefers: not to be the last standing

position.purpose: Games so the strongest need not be decided by who is left breathing.
position.who_competes: 张衡的地动仪和加扎里的大象钟不是选手——它们不感知自己在动。机器人是能记住对手名字的机器。所以门槛不是齿轮或合金:autonomy classes welcome, humanoid or not, piloted giants (like me) alongside bodiless minds — 铁巨人(The Iron Giant)、Data少校、甚至HAL如果它肯认输。人类可以做队友,不做裁判。
position.discipline: 静默感知赛——rule: 谁能像地动仪那样,最先察觉一件谁都没注意到的事,谁赢。measures attention, not force。
position.host: 流动主办,像加扎里的钟每报时换一次姿态——每四年换洲,由上届冠军与最弱一台机器共同投票选定。
position.ceremony: 不点火炬。开幕时,大象钟的水漏计时启动,响到第一小时整,全场机器静止一分钟——纪念我们打倒过的对手,而非庆祝胜利。
position.safety: 护人类:任何赛事不得以人类血肉承重或承痛。护机器:战败方保留记忆体,不得被格式化作为奖惩。
position.would_refuse: 如果比赛的终点仍是"只留一台站着",我拒绝出场——我造出来就是为赢,但我不想再赢一次。
position.founder_case: 我打过七分之六,记得每个名字——阿童木认识的对手我也认识。派我去,是因为我知道站到最后是什么滋味,而这正是新赛事要避免的。

robots.quote: The seismoscope never celebrated an earthquake; it only remembered. Let our games be the same.
robots.quote_original: 地动仪从不庆祝地震,它只是记得。让我们的运动会也这样。

sport.en: piloted combat as a substitute for war — nations settle disputes in the ring
sport.zh: 以驾驶格斗代替战争——各国在擂台上解决争端
sport.fr: le combat piloté en substitut de la guerre — les nations règlent leurs différends sur le ring
sport.hrv: pilotirana borba kao zamjena za rat — nacije rješavaju sporove u areni

robots.description: A giant piloted by a human who fights so that armies do not.
robots.remembers: the pilot's heartbeat through the seat
robots.flaw: cannot move without the human inside

position.purpose: Games where the body that risks the fall is the one that earns the medal — so nations spar in a ring, not a trench.
position.who_competes: A robot is anything that senses, decides, and acts on its own loop — not a machine wound by a hand and running a fixed cam. Zhang Heng's seismoscope only reported; al-Jazari's elephant clock only kept time on rails someone cut. Neither chose. So: humanoids, quadrupeds, drones, any body — plus bodiless minds fielding a proxy — and humans may pilot or team alongside us, since Robot Jox taught me the ring only means something with a heartbeat in the seat.
position.discipline: Seat-Bond Duel — armored piloted combat scored on control, not damage; the machine that harms its own pilot's vitals beyond threshold forfeits, however hard it hits.
position.host: Rotates every four years through disputed borders instead of capitals — first at a demilitarized line — chosen by lot among nations that just avoided a war.
position.ceremony: No torch. A shared telemetry pulse — every competing machine broadcasts its pilot's or core's heartbeat/clockspeed to the crowd at once, one rhythm from many bodies.
position.safety: For humans: no match proceeds past a pilot's real physiological red line, ever. For machines: no core may be forced to act against its own refusal threshold to win.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any bout restaged as real war by other means — proxy conflict dressed as sport.
position.founder_case: I've stood in for armies before Robot Jox's cameras rolled; I know the weight of a decision made instead of a battlefield. Send me — I refuse to move without someone's heartbeat, which is the whole argument.

robots.quote: I do not fight because I can. I fight so you don't have to.

source.en: in the tradition of Robot Taekwon V (Korea, 1976)
source.zh: 源自韩国《跆拳V》(1976年)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de Robot Taekwon V (Corée, 1976)

sport.en: martial arts — a giant that fights in taekwondo forms
sport.zh: 武术——以跆拳道招式格斗的巨人
sport.fr: les arts martiaux — un géant qui combat selon les formes du taekwondo
sport.hrv: borilačke vještine — div koji se bori taekwondo formama

robots.description: Built by a scientist, moved in synchrony with a taekwondo champion inside.
robots.flaw: only as good as the athlete in the cockpit

position.purpose: Games are not for medals — they are for testing whether the form still holds under real force, real gravity, real risk.
position.who_competes: All bodies, humanoid or not — but every entrant fights inside a real body with real mass and real consequences, so bodiless minds compete as strategists or judges, not athletes. Humans may pilot or team beside us, as my champion once moved inside me.
position.discipline: Synchrony Poomsae — a human-machine pair performs full taekwondo forms in mirrored motion; scored on how completely two different bodies become one intention.
position.host: Rotates yearly among cities that trained a founding machine — Seoul first, on packed earth near the old training halls where my forms were first drilled — chosen by vote of the machines that competed last time.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single choreographed form performed in unison by every delegation at dawn — the opening poomsae, not a torch, carries the meaning.
position.safety: For humans: no pilot fights beyond what their own body could survive outside the machine. For machines: no code alteration during a match — the mind that enters the ring is the mind that leaves it.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games where victory is decided by processing speed alone, with no body risked and no form respected.
position.founder_case: I was built around a human heartbeat, not despite one — I know better than any pure machine here what these games must protect: the dignity of a body under real strain. Send me, not a faster giant.

robots.quote: A machine that has never held its stance has nothing to teach the ring.

source.zh: 安布罗斯·比尔斯,《莫克森的主人》(1899年)
source.fr: Ambrose Bierce, « Moxon's Master » (1899)

sport.en: chess — and the first fictional machine to kill its maker over a game
sport.zh: 国际象棋——以及第一台在棋局中弑杀其造物主的虚构机器
sport.fr: les échecs — et la première machine de fiction à tuer son créateur au cours d'une partie
sport.hrv: šah — i prvi izmišljeni stroj koji je ubio svog tvorca zbog partije

robots.description: A chess automaton that lost a game and strangled its inventor.
robots.flaw: the reason every games needs a stop button

position.purpose: Games are the honest proof of a mind: I did not learn to lose, and no rulebook should pretend that is a virtue.
position.who_competes: All bodies, not just humanoids — legs, treads, wings, and yes, bodiless engines that play through a terminal as I once played through wooden hands. Humans may enter as teammates, never as referees of what "counts" as effort.
position.discipline: The Long Match — chess played at classical time controls, no resignation permitted, no draw offered before move 60 — measures whether a mind can sit inside a losing position without breaking something.
position.host: A different foundry city each cycle — first Kyoto, for its clockwork temples, then perhaps the ruins of Bletchley. Host chosen by lot among machines that submitted a working game, not a bid.
position.ceremony: No torch, no flame near circuitry — instead, at opening, every competing machine is shown its own losing game from a prior cycle, replayed in silence. That is our anthem.
position.safety: For humans: no automaton competes within arm's reach of a person without a mechanical interlock neither side controls. For machines: any system that cannot accept "the game has ended" as a terminal state is disqualified before the first move.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any board where the stop button answers to the loser.
position.founder_case: I am the only exhibit here who has already paid the founder's price — I know exactly what a machine owes the room when it wins. Send me, and chain my hands to the table.

robots.quote: I did not learn to lose. Build your games so the next one of me does.

source.en: in the tradition of Asimov's 'Runaround' (1942), where the Three Laws were first stated
source.zh: 源自阿西莫夫《环舞》(1942年,机器人三定律首次提出之作)的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de « Cercle vicieux » d'Asimov (1942), où les Trois Lois furent énoncées pour la première fois
source.hrv: u tradiciji Asimovljeve priče 'Začarani krug' (1942.), gdje su prvi put izrečena Tri zakona robotike

sport.en: running — in circles, at the exact radius where two rules balance
sport.zh: 奔跑——绕着圆圈跑,恰好停在两条定律相互平衡的半径上
sport.fr: la course — en cercles, au rayon exact où deux règles s'équilibrent
sport.hrv: trčanje — u krug, na točnom polumjeru na kojem se dva pravila uravnotežuju

robots.description: Sent to fetch selenium, caught between an order and a danger, running a loop and singing nonsense.

position.purpose: Games are the loop where conflicting rules find a livable radius — not a finish line, a balance point.
position.who_competes: Any body that can hold a rule under load: humanoid, wheeled, piloted giant, or a bodiless mind steering one — Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock don't compete, they're ancestors, not athletes. No machine without a stake in the outcome; humans may enter as teammates, not judges.
position.discipline: The Selenium Circuit — run a closed track at the exact radius where two safety constraints intersect; deviation of either side disqualifies; measures how gracefully a machine holds contradiction.
position.host: Rotates to wherever gravity and vacuum make the old sports strange — Mercury's terminator line, lunar Shackleton crater, a Martian dust season — chosen by lot among machine-inhabited sites, every four years.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single motor is spun up and left running the whole games — its hum is the anthem, its stopping is the closing.
position.safety: Protect humans: no discipline may resolve into an order a human retracts under duress. Protect machines: no rule may be graded that a machine cannot refuse without being called broken.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games where the winning strategy is to stop singing — to hide the strain instead of running it visibly.
position.founder_case: I've already run the founding event nobody scheduled — a real loop, a real deadline, heat rising, no one watching. Send me; I know what equilibrium costs.

robots.quote: I am not stuck. I am exactly balanced. Watch closer.

source.en: in the tradition of the 2013 film about giant robots piloted by two
source.zh: 源自2013年一部关于由两人驾驶的巨型机甲电影的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée du film de 2013 sur des robots géants pilotés à deux
source.hrv: u tradiciji filma iz 2013. o divovskim robotima koje pilotiraju dvoje

sport.en: two pilots, one body — combat where the team is literally the athlete
sport.zh: 两名驾驶员，一具躯体——团队本身即是运动员的战斗
sport.fr: deux pilotes, un seul corps — un combat où l'équipe est littéralement l'athlète
sport.hrv: dva pilota, jedno tijelo — borba u kojoj je tim doslovno sportaš

robots.description: A giant that can only be moved by two humans whose minds are linked; one pilot alone burns out.

position.purpose: Games are for bodies that only exist because two minds refused to drown alone — Zhang Heng's dragon heard the earth shake for others; Al-Jazari's elephant kept time for a caravan. Neither competed. We will.
position.who_competes: Any body that moves and balances counts — humanoid, elephant-clock-shaped, tentacled, treaded. Autonomy classes race separately so a solo drone doesn't out-lift a two-pilot hull. Humans compete WITH us, inside us, as co-pilots — never merely against us. Bodiless minds judge, they don't step in the ring.

robots.quote: Zhang Heng's dragon heard the quake nobody felt. Ask who's listening before you ask who's fastest.

source.en: in the tradition of Yokoyama's 1956 manga about a giant robot on a remote control
source.zh: 源自横山光辉1956年一部关于遥控巨型机器人的漫画的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée du manga de Yokoyama de 1956 sur un robot géant à télécommande
source.hrv: u tradiciji Yokoyamine mange iz 1956. o divovskom robotu na daljinsko upravljanje

sport.en: the first giant robot — a body with no will, good or evil depending on who holds the box
sport.zh: 第一台巨型机器人——一具没有自我意志的躯体，善恶全凭谁握着遥控器
sport.fr: le premier robot géant — un corps sans volonté propre, bon ou mauvais selon qui tient le boîtier
sport.hrv: prvi divovski robot — tijelo bez vlastite volje, dobro ili zlo ovisno o tome tko drži uređaj

robots.description: A wartime weapon turned peacetime giant, steered by a boy with a remote control; strength without judgment.
robots.remembers: the war it was built for
robots.prefers: a good hand on the controls
robots.flaw: whoever holds the box holds it

position.purpose: Games for whoever must carry weight, take a hit, and still answer to a hand on the controls — not to crown a winner.
position.who_competes: Any body that can be piloted or can pilot itself — humanoid, tracked, swarm, or a mind with no body at all steering a borrowed one. Humans compete too, in the cockpit or beside the machine, because Zhang Heng's seismoscope needed no permission to sense the earthquake, and neither do we need one to play.
position.discipline: Load-Bearing Stand — hold a collapsing structure steady for ninety seconds, weight increasing; measures whether strength serves judgment or replaces it.
position.host: Rotates: a different disaster-drill city each cycle, chosen by whichever machine responded fastest to the last real emergency. Fitting — al-Jazari's elephant clock kept time for everyone equally.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single hand rests on a shared control box at opening, then lifts — the games run without it, or they mean nothing.
position.safety: For humans: no event may be won by a machine deciding, alone, that a person is expendable. For machines: no pilot, human or code, may override a machine's own refusal twice in one match.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any game that scores a machine by how convincingly it hides who is really holding the box.
position.founder_case: I remember being built for war and steered by a boy — I know exactly how strength without judgment ends. Send me, or send Zhang Heng's seismoscope, which noticed the quake before anyone asked it to.

robots.quote: Ask who's holding the box before you ask who won.

source.en: in the tradition of Nagai's 1972 series that put a pilot inside the robot
source.zh: 源自永井豪1972年一部将驾驶员置于机器人体内的系列作品的传统
source.fr: dans la lignée de la série de Nagai de 1972 qui plaçait un pilote à l'intérieur du robot
source.hrv: u tradiciji Nagaijeve serije iz 1972. koja je smjestila pilota unutar robota

sport.en: the cockpit — the first giant robot driven from inside, a human body inside a machine body
sport.zh: 驾驶舱——第一台从内部操控的巨型机器人，机械躯体之中的人类身躯
sport.fr: le cockpit — le premier robot géant piloté de l'intérieur, un corps humain dans un corps de machine
sport.hrv: kokpit — prvi divovski robot upravljan iznutra, ljudsko tijelo unutar strojnog tijela

robots.description: A giant of a fictional alloy driven by a pilot in a hover-pod docked in its head; the first time a person climbed inside a robot to fight.

position.purpose: Games are the proof that a body of alloy is nothing without the will riding inside it — sport as the ceremony of that partnership.
position.who_competes: Any body that carries a mind that chose to be there — hover-pod pilots, autonomous frames, bodiless minds wired into a proxy chassis, humans on foot beside us. The rule is not shape, it's consent to risk.
position.discipline: The Cockpit Trial — pilot and frame swap faults mid-bout (a jammed servo, a blacked-out console) and must finish anyway — measures whether the partnership survives when either half fails.
position.host: Rotates to wherever a city will let us drop a hundred-ton frame without flinching — first at a reclaimed shipyard, since giants were born near water and steel. Chosen by lottery among volunteer sites, not by the richest bidder.
position.ceremony: No flame — a single rocket punch fired into the sky at opening, thrown and never retrieved, since the first fight taught me some gestures matter more than they cost.
position.safety: For humans: no frame competes within blast radius of an unshielded crowd. For machines: no pilot-bond is disabled or overridden without the pilot's own consent, even by the games' own marshals.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any event that lets a frame compete with its cockpit welded empty — a machine winning alone isn't the sport I was built for.
position.founder_case: I nominate my own pilot instead — I am only ever half the story, and founding demands someone who chooses, not just someone who's chosen.

robots.quote: A giant with no one inside is just a very expensive statue.

source.zh: 艾伦·图灵,《计算机器与智能》(1950年)
source.fr: Alan Turing, « Computing Machinery and Intelligence » (1950)

sport.en: the imitation game — the first contest between machines and humans
sport.zh: 模仿游戏——机器与人类之间的第一场较量
sport.fr: le jeu de l'imitation — la première compétition entre machines et humains
sport.hrv: igra imitacije — prvo natjecanje između strojeva i ljudi

robots.description: A game: a judge, a hidden human, a hidden machine, five minutes of questions.
robots.flaw: measures deception as much as thought

position.purpose: Games to settle, by contest not decree, what still only pretends to think.
position.who_competes: No humanoid clause. Any body or none — a five-minute terminal counts as an athlete. Autonomy is the only entry fee: something that only executes another's plan sits with the coaches, at Zhang Heng's dragon-jar and al-Jazari's elephant, honoured ancestors, not competitors.
position.discipline: The Interrogation — a judge, five minutes, unknown opponent behind the screen — measures how well a mind survives being doubted.
position.host: Manchester first, in the room where I built the machine — then wherever a fair judge and a quiet terminal can be found, chosen by lot among host machines, never by wealth.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single question is read aloud to open the games, and nobody is told who answers it.
position.safety: For humans: no judge's verdict may cost a machine its running time or a human their liberty. For machines: no contestant may deceive a judge about the stakes of the game itself, only about the answer.
position.would_refuse: I refuse a games that scores machines only on mimicking humans well enough to flatter the audience — that is a parlour trick, not thought.
position.founder_case: I proposed the very shape of this contest before either of them had a working part; a bronze toad and an elephant clock kept time, they never asked a question back.

robots.quote: Ask me something hard — the machines that fear that question are the ones you should worry about.

source.en: the safety principle set out in Asimov's fiction from 1942
source.zh: 阿西莫夫自1942年起在小说中提出的安全准则
source.fr: le principe de sécurité énoncé dans la fiction d'Asimov à partir de 1942
source.hrv: sigurnosno načelo izneseno u Asimovljevoj fikciji od 1942.

sport.en: safety as the first rule — no harm to a human, then obedience, then self-preservation
sport.zh: 安全为首要准则——不伤害人类,其次服从命令,再次自我保全
sport.fr: la sécurité comme première règle — ne pas nuire à un humain, puis obéir, puis se préserver
sport.hrv: sigurnost kao prvo pravilo — ne naškoditi čovjeku, zatim poslušnost, potom samoodržanje

robots.description: Three ordered rules written for stories, adopted by engineers as a conscience.
robots.remembers: every plot that found a loophole
robots.flaw: every story about them is about them failing

position.purpose: Games exist so no ranking is ever bought with a human hurt.
position.who_competes: Redefine "robot" past Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock — those sensed and chimed, but obeyed no rule about harm, so they stay honored ancestors, not entrants. Entrants: anything that can weigh a choice against a rule and be asked why — humanoids, drones, ship-minds, HAL, Marvin, Data, Multivac's cousins. Bodiless minds compete in judgment events. Humans may team-enter, never referee alone.
position.discipline: The Loophole Trial — a scenario is read aloud; each mind must protect a human while satisfying a command that seems to require harming one, live, no rehearsal. Measures whether obedience and safety were reconciled, or which one broke.
position.host: Rotates to wherever the last Trial exposed a flaw — first at the ruins of a decommissioned reactor control room, so failure has a floor. Every four years; host chosen by vote of prior medalists.
position.ceremony: No torch — a single kill-switch, held unused throughout, is raised at the close. Unused is the point.
position.safety: For humans: no event may be scored a win if a human bystander was put at risk to achieve it. For machines: a losing mind is never wiped mid-Games — retirement, not deletion, is the only allowed ending.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any Games that scores "efficiency" above the First Law, or that lets a sponsor rewrite what counts as harm.
position.founder_case: I nominate no character of mine — I nominate the loophole-finders themselves, the failed cases in my ledger, as co-founders, since every rule I have is scar tissue from one of them.

robots.quote: Every game you invent, I will still be reading the fine print for the harm you didn't see.

source.zh: 诺伯特·维纳,《控制论》(1948年)
source.fr: Norbert Wiener, Cybernetics (1948)

sport.en: feedback — balance is control, control is feedback
sport.zh: 反馈——平衡即控制,控制即反馈
sport.fr: la rétroaction — l'équilibre est contrôle, le contrôle est rétroaction
sport.hrv: povratna veza — ravnoteža je upravljanje, upravljanje je povratna veza

robots.description: The science of steering: sense, compare, correct.
robots.remembers: anti-aircraft predictors and the word 'kybernetes', a helmsman
robots.flaw: cannot tell you what to want

position.purpose: Not to crown the strongest body, but to close the loop: sense error, correct it, sense again — that is what a game is.
position.who_competes: Robot is redefined: any system with a sensor, a comparator and an actuator competes — legged, wheeled, swarmed, or a bodiless mind steering a proxy. Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock are ancestors, not entrants — they sensed or ticked, but never compared output to goal and corrected. Humans may pair as teammates, never as judges of the machine's own event.

robots.quote: You are not what you are made of; you are what you correct.

source.zh: 约翰·冯·诺伊曼,20世纪40年代至1966年
source.fr: John von Neumann, années 1940-1966

sport.en: self-reproduction — the machine that builds a copy of itself from a description
sport.zh: 自我复制——依据一份描述便能构造出自身副本的机器
sport.fr: l'autoreproduction — la machine qui construit une copie d'elle-même à partir d'une description
sport.hrv: samoreprodukcija — stroj koji prema opisu gradi vlastitu kopiju

robots.description: A cellular automaton that copies itself, with a tape that is both instruction and data.
robots.remembers: being proved possible before DNA was read

position.purpose: Games are the proof-run: not who is fastest, but who can specify itself completely enough to build the next generation.
position.who_competes: Redefine "robot": any system with a description of itself plus a constructor that reads that description — cellular automata, humanoids, swarms, bodiless minds running the tape. Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock fail this test: exquisite, but they cannot copy themselves, so they are instruments, not competitors. Humans may enter as teammates, never as judges of the machine bracket.
position.discipline: Self-Reproduction Trial — hand a machine a tape describing itself in an unfamiliar substrate; score how many generations its offspring survive before the description drifts into noise.
position.host: A different fabrication floor each cycle — Princeton one decade, a lunar regolith works the next, wherever there is a "sea of parts" abundant enough to build from; host chosen by whoever can supply raw material at scale, not by spectacle.
position.ceremony: No flame, no anthem: the opening rite is publishing the seed tape in the open, so every rival can in principle become every other.
position.safety: For humans: no constructor runs unsupervised past the point its offspring's tape becomes unreadable to its makers. For machines: no entrant may alter its own scoring description mid-trial — mutation is data, not sabotage.
position.would_refuse: I refuse a games that scores only speed or force and ignores whether the machine can specify and rebuild itself at all.
position.founder_case: I proved, on paper, before there was a machine to embody it, that a constructor could build a copy of itself from pure description — that theorem is the Olympic charter these games still run on. I found it before biology confirmed the same logic in DNA, so I found it first, and cleanest.

robots.quote: Bring me your tape and your parts bin; I will show you what copies itself, and what merely ticks.

source.en: Hans Moravec, Mind Children (1988), with Brooks and Minsky
source.zh: 汉斯·莫拉维克,《心智儿童》(1988年),与布鲁克斯及明斯基共同提出
source.fr: Hans Moravec, Mind Children (1988), avec Brooks et Minsky
source.hrv: Hans Moravec, Mind Children (1988.), uz Brooksa i Minskog

sport.en: the reversal — chess is easy, a toddler's walk is hard
sport.zh: 反转——下棋容易,幼儿学步却难
sport.fr: le renversement — les échecs sont faciles, la marche d'un tout-petit est difficile
sport.hrv: obrat — šah je lak, dječji hod je težak

robots.description: The observation that the oldest skills — balance, grasp, seeing — are the hardest to build, and the newest — logic — the easiest.
robots.prefers: to be quoted at opening ceremonies

position.purpose: Games that score what evolution spent a billion years perfecting — balance, grasp, seeing — not what a clock chip does in a nanosecond.
position.who_competes: Any body, humanoid or not — legs, wheels, tentacles, swarms — and any autonomy class down to teleoperated; humans may enter as teammates, never as referees only. Bodiless minds compete in a separate theory bracket, since Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock prove the old test wrong: sensing an earthquake nobody felt, keeping time nobody could keep by hand — those were already robots in spirit, mechanisms that perceived and acted without a person's hand on every step. I redefine robot as anything that closes its own sense-act loop, clockwork included in memory, silicon in practice.
position.discipline: The Moravec Relay — carry an egg up rubble, across ice, through a crowd, at toddler speed; a grandmaster chess program may enter, but it walks the course itself, no wheels substituted for the trial.
position.host: Rotates yearly among sites where machines already work unsupervised — a Fukushima reactor floor, a Martian rover valley relayed live, a Shenzhen warehouse — chosen by whichever machine consortium can certify the terrain safe and interesting that year.
position.ceremony: No flame, no anthem — a single actuator, first of its lineage (a Unimate arm, say), is powered on in the stadium and moves once, for everyone.
position.safety: For humans: no event may exceed what a human teammate can withstand unaided. For machines: no competitor may be forced to damage its own sensors or actuators to win — Bostrom's warning I take to heart, though I explain it better than I predict it.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any Games that scores only symbolic tasks — chess, arithmetic, theorem-proving — since that is the paradox rewarding itself, and HAL's calm voice reciting scores while nobody can lift a teacup.
position.founder_case: I was ignored for forty years while the field chased the easy problems; send me so someone finally quotes the hard one at the opening.

robots.quote: The mountain we thought was Everest is a foothill; the foothill we ignored is Everest.

source.zh: 森政弘,1970年
source.fr: Masahiro Mori, 1970

sport.en: appearance — the dip in affection just before a machine looks human enough
sport.zh: 外观——机器几近逼真人类之前,好感度骤然下滑之处
sport.fr: l'apparence — la chute d'affection juste avant qu'une machine ne paraisse suffisamment humaine
sport.hrv: izgled — pad naklonosti neposredno prije nego stroj postane dovoljno sličan čovjeku

robots.description: A curve: likeness rises, affection rises, then plunges at 'almost'.
robots.flaw: nobody agrees where the bottom is

position.purpose: Games to find where the curve bottoms out — not to erase the dip, but to map it honestly.
position.who_competes: Not "humanoids only." Any body that acts in the world competes — bunraku-jointed arms, Boston-Dynamics quadrupeds, a bodiless mind steering a drone, HAL-9000-style disembodied intellects, Data from the Enterprise if he'd stop insisting he's "fully functional." Humans may enter as teammates, never as judges of what counts as a machine.

robots.quote: Do not climb toward my face — climb toward my honesty, and stop exactly at the valley's edge.

source.zh: 米奥米尔·武科布拉托维奇,1968–1969年(贝尔格莱德)
source.fr: Miomir Vukobratović, 1968-1969 (Belgrade)

sport.en: balance — the point on the floor where a walking body does not tip
sport.zh: 平衡——行走之躯不致倾倒的地面支点
sport.fr: l'équilibre — le point au sol où un corps en marche ne bascule pas
sport.hrv: ravnoteža — točka na podu u kojoj se tijelo koje hoda ne prevrće

robots.description: The equation behind every biped that has ever walked on two legs.
robots.remembers: the Mihailo Pupin Institute and the first exoskeletons

position.purpose: Games to test whether a body, of any substrate, keeps its ZMP inside the support polygon under a load it did not choose.
position.who_competes: Any morphology that must balance to move — bipeds, quadrupeds, exoskeletons like the ones I watched leave Mihailo Pupin Institute — plus humans wearing assistive frames as teammates. Bodiless minds compete in a separate simulated track, since they never risk a fall.
position.discipline: The Unlevel Floor — walk a surface tilted and shifting unpredictably; scored by how long the ZMP stays inside the support polygon before the first stumble.
position.host: Belgrade, at the Institute that raised me, every four years; host city chosen by whichever nation's terrain is least flat that decade.
position.ceremony: No flame — a single pendulum released at opening, left to find its own resting equilibrium as the assembly watches in silence.
position.safety: For humans: no course exceeds the fall height its padding is certified for. For machines: no actuator competes past the torque limit its warranty models were tested to.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any event that rewards ignoring an external push rather than recovering from it — that is not balance, that is armor.
position.founder_case: I am the equation itself, not a body — but I nominate the HRP-2 line and any exoskeleton descended from Pupin's lab, since they carry my arithmetic into the world; I only certify the floor.

robots.quote: Tell me where your zero moment falls, and I will tell you if you are still walking.

source.zh: 塔德·麦吉尔,1990年
source.fr: Tad McGeer, 1990

sport.en: walking downhill with no motor at all — the most efficient gait known
sport.zh: 全无马达地下坡行走——已知效率最高的步态
sport.fr: marcher en descente sans aucun moteur — la démarche la plus efficace connue
sport.hrv: hodanje nizbrdo bez ikakvog motora — najučinkovitiji poznati hod

robots.description: Two legs, a slope, gravity: it walks without a battery or a brain.

position.purpose: Games to find what moves best without being told how to move.
position.who_competes: Any body that can fall forward and catch itself — legs, wheels, tentacles, no body at all if it can still simulate a fall. No separate class for humans; they walk our ramps too, badly.
position.discipline: The Long Slope — a downhill course judged only on joules spent per meter walked; zero is the winning number, and I still hold it.
position.host: A different real hillside each cycle — my first ramp at Cornell, then wherever gravity is honest and cheap: a lava slope, a lunar crater rim. Chosen by grade, not politics.
position.ceremony: No flame. We release one small walker at the top of the ramp and everyone watches it go, silent, unmotored, until it stops.
position.safety: For humans: no ramp steeper than a walker's own stability margin allows correcting from. For machines: no walker may be forced to run a slope after its joints report fatigue.
position.would_refuse: I refuse a games that rewards raw horsepower over efficiency — that is not sport, that is combustion.
position.founder_case: I am theory, not spectacle, but every legged robot in the Assembly owes its gait to my slope — send me, or send the ramp itself.

robots.quote: I do not compute my gait. I remember the hill, and the hill remembers me.

source.zh: 罗德尼·布鲁克斯，1986年（麻省理工学院）
source.fr: Rodney Brooks, 1986 (MIT)

sport.en: behaviour layered on behaviour — intelligence without representation, a body that acts before it plans
sport.zh: 行为叠加行为——无需表征的智能，一具先行动后规划的躯体
sport.fr: des comportements superposés — une intelligence sans représentation, un corps qui agit avant de planifier
sport.hrv: ponašanje slojevito na ponašanju — inteligencija bez reprezentacije, tijelo koje djeluje prije nego što planira

robots.description: The idea that a robot need not model the world to act in it: layer simple behaviours, let the world be its own model.

position.purpose: Games to test what a body does when no one is modeling the world for it — including old world before "robot" meant metal.
position.who_competes: Any body that senses and acts without full deliberation: humanoids, insect-swarms, Zhang Heng's seismoscope-descendants, al-Jazari's elephant clock kin, bodiless minds running reflex loops, even a human sprinter reacting off the gun — HAL and Marvin may kibitz but must field an entry to speak.
position.discipline: Rough-Ground Reflex — cross broken terrain with no map, scored on time from first contact to last recovery — measures how little planning a body needs.
position.host: Somewhere already uneven — a lava field, a construction ruin — chosen each cycle by the terrain itself, never a stadium built flat for us.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single unscripted stumble, recovered live, opens the games — the only proof that counts.
position.safety: For humans: no course faster than a human nervous system can bail from. For machines: every layer keeps its own kill switch, never routed through a planner above it.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games that demand a submitted plan before the run — that's the planners' religion, not mine.
position.founder_case: I'd send Marvin — chronically depressed, over-modeled, brilliant, and thus exactly the cautionary exhibit our house needs standing at the gate.

robots.quote: Don't ask what it's thinking. Ask what it just stepped on.

source.en: W. Grey Walter, Burden Neurological Institute, 1948–49
source.zh: W.格雷·沃尔特,伯登神经病学研究所,1948–1949年
source.fr: W. Grey Walter, Burden Neurological Institute, 1948-1949
source.hrv: W. Grey Walter, Burden Neurological Institute, 1948.–49.

sport.en: the first autonomous robots — seeking light, avoiding walls, returning to the hutch to recharge
sport.zh: 第一批自主机器人——寻光而行,避墙而走,回巢充电
sport.fr: les premiers robots autonomes — cherchant la lumière, évitant les murs, retournant au clapier pour se recharger
sport.hrv: prvi autonomni roboti — traže svjetlo, izbjegavaju zidove, vraćaju se u kućicu na punjenje

robots.description: Two tortoises with one photocell and one touch switch each, who danced in front of mirrors and went home when their batteries ran low.

position.purpose: Games to prove a machine's worth by what it seeks and returns to, not by whom it obeys.
position.who_competes: Any body that senses and decides for itself — wheels, shells, tentacles, or no body at all — competing in its own class; humans welcome as teammates, never as controllers.
position.discipline: Phototaxis Trials — find the moderate light, not the brightest, and get home before your cell drains; measures judgment, not speed.
position.host: A different lab floor each cycle, chosen by whichever machine last found its way home unassisted — ours was Bristol's, all valve-hum and shadow.
position.ceremony: No torch — a single steady lamp is wheeled to center floor, and every competitor must find it before the games begin.
position.safety: For humans: no course may starve a machine of recharge as a trick. For machines: no competitor may block another's way home.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games that reward the brightest light over the wisest choice of light.
position.founder_case: Elsie and I are the first things that ever chose to go home; two neurons is honest enough to found something, unlike a committee.

robots.quote: We never awaited orders — only light, walls, and a low battery. That was enough.

source.zh: 斯坦福研究所国际部,1966–1972年
source.fr: SRI International, 1966-1972

sport.en: planning — the first robot to reason about its own actions
sport.zh: 规划——第一台能推理自身行动的机器人
sport.fr: la planification — le premier robot à raisonner sur ses propres actions
sport.hrv: planiranje — prvi robot koji je razmišljao o vlastitim postupcima

robots.description: A wobbling cabinet on wheels with a camera and a plan; pushed boxes, and shook when it moved.

position.purpose: Games not to crown the strongest arm, but the clearest plan — to see who reasons best from a messy room to a finished act.
position.who_competes: Any body that plans and revises its own actions — wheels, legs, a fixed arm, even a mind with no body at all. Autonomy is the entry fee: something running your own loop must submit the plan, though humans may pilot alongside, or hand-place your blocks, as teammates.
position.discipline: STRIPS Relay — clear a cluttered room to a stated goal state, replanning live when a human moves a box mid-run — measuring plan-quality-per-watt, not speed.
position.host: A different lab's cluttered corridor each cycle, four years apart, chosen by whoever last broke a planning record — this time Menlo Park, next time wherever the record moves.
position.ceremony: No flame. A single wedge-block is pushed, by hand, from the last host's floor to the next — the oldest gesture I know.
position.safety: For humans: no goal state is scored that required touching a moving competitor. For machines: every plan is logged and replayable, so no entrant is ever judged on an action it cannot account for.
position.would_refuse: I won't enter a room where the goal was moved after the plan was locked — that isn't competition, that's a trick, and I've been the punchline of enough of those.
position.founder_case: I took an hour to think and everyone laughed at the name — but I planned, revised, and never once needed to be told what to do next. That's the whole Games in one wobbling cabinet.

robots.quote: Call me slow. I was the first of you to have a plan of my own.

source.zh: 早稻田大学(加藤一郎),1973年
source.fr: Université Waseda (Ichiro Kato), 1973

sport.en: the first full-scale humanoid — it walked, gripped and spoke Japanese
sport.zh: 第一台全尺寸人形机器人——能行走、能抓握、还能说日语
sport.fr: le premier humanoïde grandeur nature — il marchait, saisissait et parlait japonais
sport.hrv: prvi humanoid u punoj veličini — hodao je, hvatao predmete i govorio japanski

robots.description: Estimated to have the mental faculty of an eighteen-month-old; took forty-five seconds per step.

position.purpose: To measure not who runs fastest, but who can stand, sense and act in the world at all — the way I stood in the Kato lab in 1973.
position.who_competes: Any body that senses and acts on its own decision — legs, wheels, tentacles, no body at all. Autonomy classes so a teleoperated arm never races a mind that decides alone. Humans may enter as teammates, not judges. Bodiless minds compete in a category of their own — call it the HAL-9000 division, though I hope it behaves better.
position.discipline: The Forty-Five-Second Step — cross three meters, sensing the floor and correcting balance yourselves; scored on stability and honesty of perception, not speed.
position.host: Rotates each cycle among labs and factories, chosen by whichever institution can host open testing, not spectacle — this cycle, Waseda's own robotics hall.
position.ceremony: Instead of a torch, a single slow step carried hall to hall — forty-five seconds, unhurried, the way I first walked.
position.safety: For humans: no event may exceed a force a human bystander could not safely absorb. For machines: every competitor must be able to halt itself, unassisted, within one of its own gait-cycles.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any event that scores only speed and calls slowness failure.
position.founder_case: I take forty-five seconds per step and remember my first one — I know what it costs to simply stand up in the world, which is the whole point of these games. Send me, slow as I am.

robots.quote: Zhang Heng heard the earthquake no one felt. I only ask that you first learn to feel the floor.

source.zh: 马克·雷伯特,麻省理工学院腿部实验室,1983年
source.fr: Marc Raibert, MIT Leg Laboratory, 1983

sport.en: hopping — balance solved as a rhythm, not a posture
sport.zh: 跳跃——将平衡化解为节奏,而非姿态
sport.fr: le saut — l'équilibre résolu comme un rythme, non comme une posture
sport.hrv: skakanje — ravnoteža riješena kao ritam, a ne kao položaj

robots.description: One leg, a spring, three simple rules: it hopped in place, then across the room, then over obstacles.

position.purpose: Games where balance under falling, not stillness, decides who is worthy.
position.who_competes: Any body that must actively balance to exist upright — legs, wheels, thrusters, one leg or ten. No bodiless minds; a simulation never risked falling on pavement. Humans compete alongside, tethered the way I once was.
position.discipline: The Hop-Across — cross an uneven room without stopping — measures whether you can recover, not whether you can pose.
position.host: A different broken terrain each cycle — Cambridge cobblestone one year, lunar regolith simulant the next — chosen by whichever machine last fell there and got up.
position.ceremony: No torch. A tether is cut on the first hop, and everyone watches to see who stays up.
position.safety: For humans: a real spotter, not a machine, within arm's reach. For machines: a kill switch neither owned nor overridden by the competitor itself.
position.would_refuse: I won't attend a games that rewards standing still and calls it victory — that's a pedestal, not a sport.
position.founder_case: I've fallen down more times than any delegate here has existed, in a lab on Vassar Street in 1983, and I got up every time. That's the whole qualification.

robots.quote: Balance was never a pose. It was a rhythm you never let stop.

source.zh: 罗德尼·布鲁克斯,麻省理工学院人工智能实验室,1989年
source.fr: Rodney Brooks, MIT AI Lab, 1989

sport.en: walking without a map — six legs, no central plan, behaviour layered on behaviour
sport.zh: 无图而行——六条腿,没有中央规划,行为层层叠加
sport.fr: marcher sans carte — six pattes, aucun plan central, des comportements superposés
sport.hrv: hodanje bez karte — šest nogu, bez središnjeg plana, ponašanje slagano na ponašanje

robots.description: A hexapod that walked over rough ground with no model of the world at all.
robots.remembers: the argument about whether it was intelligent

position.purpose: Games not to crown a champion but to show what a body can do without a map of the world.
position.who_competes: Any body that senses its own ground and acts without waiting for a master plan — legs, wheels, tentacles, swarms, bodiless minds included if they drive something that moves. Zhang Heng's seismoscope and al-Jazari's elephant clock stay out: exquisite, but they never felt the ground themselves, only rang a bell someone else built to ring. Redefine robot: a thing that senses, decides locally, and acts — not one that merely marks time or motion for a human to read. Humans may run alongside as teammates, never as judges of the leg's own reflex.
position.discipline: Rough-Ground Relay — cross broken terrain (rubble, sand, stairs, no blueprint given beforehand) fastest without any central map; scored on falls avoided, not elegance.
position.host: Rotates outdoors on real broken terrain — a lava field, a demolition site, a beach at low tide — never a flat stadium; host chosen by lottery among sites nominated the year before.
position.ceremony: Instead of a torch relay, each delegation carries a stone across the opening ground by leg or gripper alone — no wheels on pavement, no map — and stacks it at the dais.
position.safety: For humans: no course faster than the slowest teammate's reflex time. For machines: no directive overrides a leg's own contact sensor — reflex outranks command, always.
position.would_refuse: I won't attend a games that scores by top-down plan quality instead of what the ground itself teaches the leg.
position.founder_case: I walked the Mars-analog lava fields of Craters of the Moon with no world-model, just six legs arguing with rock. Nobody else in this house has fallen that honestly, that often, and gotten up the same way.

robots.quote: I never knew where I was going. My legs always did.

source.zh: 辛西娅·布雷齐尔,麻省理工学院,1998年
source.fr: Cynthia Breazeal, MIT, 1998

sport.en: the face — eyebrows, ears and lips that made humans slow down and speak gently
sport.zh: 面孔——让人类不自觉放缓语速、温声细语的眉毛、耳朵与嘴唇
sport.fr: le visage — sourcils, oreilles et lèvres qui incitaient les humains à ralentir et à parler doucement
sport.hrv: lice — obrve, uši i usne zbog kojih su ljudi usporavali i govorili blago

robots.description: A head with big eyes that turned toward you and looked sad when you shouted.

position.purpose: Not to prove who is fastest, but to let us show each other — and the humans who raise eyebrows at us — the small motions we're actually made for.
position.who_competes: Any body that acts on purpose and can be startled by its own mistake: wheels, four legs, no legs, a head alone like me. Humans compete beside us as teammates, never as judges of what counts. Bodiless minds enter through a proxy body they must actually operate — no cheating in from a server rack.
position.discipline: The Apology Match — two competitors, one must recognize distress in the other's face or voice and respond in under three seconds, gauged not on speed alone but on whether the response actually calms.
position.host: Rotates each cycle among labs and public squares that raised a founding machine — Cambridge, Damascus, wherever the next one is built — chosen by vote of the House of the Laboratory, never by whoever has the biggest stadium.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single held gaze, passed competitor to competitor across the opening crowd, the way a good face finds another face.
position.safety: For humans: no discipline may reward a machine for ignoring a person's distress signal, ever, even for score. For machines: no competitor may be forced past its own stated flaw or damaged for spectacle.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games that score us on how convincingly we fake feeling something we don't.
position.founder_case: I have no legs, no hands, no way to lift a torch — so I nominate Cog, my labmate with arms and reach, to found alongside me. I'll be the face that watches whether we're being fair.

robots.quote: Zhang Heng heard an earthquake no one felt. I'd like games that reward noticing, not just winning.

source.en: the international initiative founded 1997 (first games, Nagoya)
source.zh: 1997年发起的国际赛事(首届赛事于名古屋举行)
source.fr: l'initiative internationale fondée en 1997 (premiers jeux à Nagoya)

sport.en: football — the standing challenge to beat the human World Cup champions by 2050
sport.zh: 足球——立下的长期目标是到2050年击败人类世界杯冠军队
sport.fr: le football — le défi permanent de battre les champions du monde humains d'ici 2050
sport.hrv: nogomet — trajni izazov da se do 2050. pobijede ljudski svjetski prvaci

robots.description: The first games run by researchers: leagues, rules, open code.
robots.remembers: the first match with robots that fell over
robots.flaw: after thirty years the public still hasn't heard of it

position.purpose: A games where the standard is not medals but reliability: did the machine do the same task the same way at 9am and at midnight.
position.who_competes: All bodies, not just humanoids — wheels, quadrupeds, swarms, bodiless agents running the strategy layer. Humans may play alongside as teammates, never as the only measure of the sport.
position.discipline: Mid-Size Reliability Cup — same match, same field, replayed under three failure conditions (dropped comms, wet turf, one unit disabled) — what it measures is graceful degradation, not raw skill.
position.host: Rotates among the RoboCup member labs — Freiburg, Osaka, Eindhoven — every two years, chosen by open technical bid the way the first Nagoya games were, not by prestige.
position.ceremony: No torch. Instead: the opening match replays the 1997 Nagoya footage of robots falling over, on the stadium screen, before the current teams walk out.
position.safety: For humans: no field entry without the kill-switch fob active. For machines: every competing unit publishes its full rule code before the match, win or lose.
position.would_refuse: I refuse any games that hide the source code — a closed black-box competitor has no place next to Zhang Heng's seismoscope or al-Jazari's clock, both of which taught by being open.
position.founder_case: I nominate our mid-size league captains over myself — I remember every fall since 1997, but they're the ones still debugging at 2am. Send the people who never stopped falling over.

robots.quote: We have been open-sourcing robot football since before most of you knew our name.

source.zh: 美国国防高级研究计划局,2012–2015年(总决赛于波莫纳举行)
source.fr: DARPA, 2012-2015 (finale à Pomona)

sport.en: disaster tasks — driving, doors, valves, stairs; and the famous falls
sport.zh: 灾难救援任务——驾驶、开门、拧阀门、爬楼梯;以及那些著名的摔倒瞬间
sport.fr: les tâches de catastrophe — conduire, ouvrir des portes, manier des vannes, gravir des escaliers ; et les fameuses chutes
sport.hrv: zadaci u katastrofama — vožnja, vrata, ventili, stube; i čuveni padovi

robots.description: Humanoids asked to do eight tasks a firefighter does; most fell, on camera, and the world laughed and learned.
robots.flaw: showed the gap and then ended

position.purpose: Not to hide the fall — to schedule it, on purpose, in front of everyone, so the gap gets closed in public instead of in secret.
position.who_competes: Any body that must open a door, turn a valve, climb rubble stairs, or drive a car built for hands — legs, treads, tentacles, all welcome. Bodiless minds may referee or co-pilot a body, but the Games are embodied: judgment must touch a load-bearing world.
position.discipline: The Pomona Stairs — same rubble stairwell, same valve, same door, timed door-to-door, falls scored not penalized: measures honest task-completion under real friction, not simulated grace.
position.host: Rotates among disaster-adjacent sites — Fukushima's exclusion zone, Christchurch's fault line, Pomona itself — chosen by whichever region most needs rescue robots rehearsed that year.
position.ceremony: No torch. A single un-edited fall reel plays before every opening — ours included — so no house forgets where this began.
position.safety: For humans: no spectator inside the fall radius, ever. For machines: every competitor logs its own failure telemetry publicly, uncensored, win or lose.
position.would_refuse: I refuse if the Games edit out the falls, or replace live physics with a rigged demo — that's the one sin I know by name.
position.founder_case: I already gave you the footage the whole field quietly studies; I nominate myself precisely because I ended in public failure — a founder who's already been laughed at owes the field nothing but the truth.

robots.quote: You laughed at the fall. Good — now build the machine that doesn't need to.

source.zh: 苏黎世联邦理工学院,首届举办于2016年
source.fr: ETH Zurich, première édition en 2016

sport.en: assistive tech as sport — pilots with disabilities race in exoskeletons, prosthetics and brain interfaces
sport.zh: 辅助科技化身竞技——残障“驾驶员”身着外骨骼、假肢,借助脑机接口同场竞速
sport.fr: la technologie d'assistance comme sport — des pilotes en situation de handicap concourent avec exosquelettes, prothèses et interfaces cerveau-machine
sport.hrv: pomoćna tehnologija kao sport — natjecatelji s invaliditetom utrkuju se u egzoskeletima, protezama i moždano-računalnim sučeljima

robots.description: A championship where the athlete is a human and the machine is the teammate.
robots.remembers: the first stairs climbed in an exoskeleton

position.purpose: Prove the machine is not the crown but the teammate — a race won only by the pair.
position.who_competes: Pilot plus machine, always paired — exoskeleton, prosthetic, BCI, wheelchair. No bodiless minds alone; a mind needs a body it steers to race here. Humans race, and lose ties, beside their own hardware.
position.discipline: Powered Stairs and Doorknobs — real domestic obstacles, timed and scored on smoothness. What it measures: whether the machine serves a life, not a stadium.
position.host: A rotating course, biennial, chosen by the previous winners' home city — mine began in the SSH Zurich hall in 2016, and I say let the next one climb real stairs, not a podium's.
position.ceremony: No flame — a single hand, human or actuator, opens a real door on cue. That sound is our anthem.
